summary.intent: Fix two failing E2E tests in CI (batch-download and streaming-playback) and investigate a release-gate timeout issue.
summary.outcome: Both E2E tests were patched with warm-up/retry logic and SW readiness checks and committed to a feature branch. The release-gate issue was diagnosed as a stale workflow reference on the release-please PR branch that will self-resolve on next rebase.

repo: The workflow formerly named e2e.yml was renamed to ci-e2e.yml in commit 2eec5ad (PR #396), and web-e2e.yml is the Playwright-specific workflow.
release-gate.yml polls --workflow=ci-e2e.yml on main; the release-please PR branch still had the old --workflow=e2e.yml reference, causing 30-attempt poll timeouts.
The .video-cipher-badge element only renders when isStreaming is true, which requires both the decrypt Service Worker to be active AND the file metadata to report CTR encryption mode.
batch-download.spec.ts is alphabetically first among E2E tests and its beforeAll login runs cold in CI, making it prone to page-closed errors during wallet login.
The decrypt-sw.ts Service Worker uses clients.claim()/skipWaiting patterns; SW activation in CI is not guaranteed before test assertions fire.
The decrypt progress test in streaming-playback.spec.ts already uses soft/catch-based assertions to handle SW-not-active gracefully.

code.finding: beforeAll loginViaWallet fails with 'Target page, context or browser has been closed' on CI cold start; fixed with warm-up navigation and retry logic.
.video-cipher-badge locator timed out after 15s; fixed by adding a SW readiness check before asserting on the badge and increasing timeout.
isStreaming flag gates the badge render; depends on isSwActive state derived from SW registration.
On the release-please PR branch this line referenced --workflow=e2e.yml (now stale); main already has --workflow=ci-e2e.yml.

workflow: gh CLI can be used to fetch CI job logs and parse them with jq to diagnose failures without leaving the terminal.
When a workflow is renamed, any long-lived branches (like release-please PRs) that reference the old workflow name by string will silently fail until rebased.
Checking alphabetical test ordering matters for cold-start flakiness diagnosis in Playwright CI runs.

friction: CI logs were truncated, requiring multiple targeted bash queries to extract the actual test failure summary.
The session hit usage limits mid-investigation, interrupting work between the diagnosis and the fix phases.
Tracing the release-gate timeout required many sequential gh CLI calls to correlate run timing, SHAs, and workflow names across multiple workflow files.
open_items: The release-please PR branch (#384 area) still has the stale --workflow=e2e.yml reference; it will self-resolve on next push to main triggering a rebase, but should be monitored.
The E2E fixes were committed to a feature branch but not yet pushed or PR'd — follow-up needed to open and merge the PR.
The root cause of the batch-download cold-start crash (loginViaWallet page closure) was mitigated with retry logic but not fully diagnosed; may recur under heavier CI load.
SW activation timing in CI is inherently flaky for streaming tests; a more robust solution would be an explicit SW-ready gate in test setup rather than per-test waits.
